slides.heading: Suffix Trie Construction
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Tries
slides.narration: Let's solve Suffix Trie Construction, a medium tries problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Build a trie of all suffixes (terminated by '*') and answer contains(suffix).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Build a trie of all suffixes (terminated by ' ') and answer contains(suffix).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Insert every suffix into a trie, then any substring is a path from the root.
slides.narration: Insert every suffix into a trie, then any substring is a path from the root.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Store suffixes in a list → O(n·m) lookup
Suffix trie → O(n²) build, O(m) lookup
slides.narration: Storing suffixes in a list makes each lookup scan everything. A suffix trie builds in quadratic time and space and answers lookups in the length of the query.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. For each start index, insert the suffix
slides.narration: Step by step. First, for each start index, insert the suffix. Second, mark ends with a star. Third, contains walks the trie.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Insert suffix 'babc'
slides.narration: Insert the suffix b a b c, followed by an end marker.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Insert suffix 'abc'
slides.narration: Insert the suffix a b c, followed by an end marker.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Insert suffix 'bc'
slides.narration: Insert the suffix b c, followed by an end marker.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Insert suffix 'c'
slides.narration: Insert the suffix c, followed by an end marker.

slides.heading: Worked example

lines: contains('abc'): b? no — a → b → c → * ✓

slides.caption: Lookup walks the trie, then checks the end marker
slides.narration: Contains walks the characters; it's true only if the final node has the end marker, so ab is not a suffix but abc is.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: The constructor inserts every suffix character by character, creating nodes as needed, then adds the end marker. Contains walks the characters and checks the end marker.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is build O of n squared, contains O of m. Space is O of n squared.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: End marker distinguishes suffix from substring
slides.narration: The end marker distinguishes a true suffix from just a substring.

slides.narration: Mention suffix trees and arrays for linear-space alternatives.

bullets: Insert every suffix into a trie, then any substring is a path from the root.
slides.narration: To recap Suffix Trie Construction: Insert every suffix into a trie, then any substring is a path from the root. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
